subject: LedgerOne discovery — cost/TCO recap and ops asks
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Huang <sara@ledgerone.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: LedgerOne discovery — cost/TCO recap and ops asks

Hi Sara — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from my side so we have alignment before we put together a formal pilot proposal. Please skim and confirm anything I missed.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- High volume of semantic search & embeddings for product catalog (expect ~120M embedding requests/month during peak).
- Chat/assistant for internal ops with 95th latency SLO ~150ms for short answers (goal: under 200ms to keep UX snappy).
- Current target budget for a 3-month pilot: ~$30k/month all-in (customer has flexibility if ROI is clear but procurement wants a capped commit).
- Primary success metrics: (1) 70% reduction in latency vs current CPU-based infra, (2) cost per 1k embeddings <= $X (we'll estimate), (3) qualitative accuracy for retrieval-augmented answers.

Cost levers we discussed
- Batching & continuous batching: significant per-token savings for embedding flows — depends on acceptable tail latency.
- KV/prefix caching for repeated context in chat flows (saves decoder tokens).
- Quantized model variants (int8 / q4_0) can reduce GPU footprint, with small accuracy delta we can measure in evals.
- Dedicated vs hosted routing: dedicated capacity gives predictability for SLA but has commit requirements.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm the 120M/month embedding rough figure and whether there are predictable daily patterns (spikes vs steady)?
2) Procurement asked for a capped pilot price. Would $30k/mo be a hard ceiling or a target we can stretch?
3) Security: they wanted SOC2 evidence and a brief on data retention — I attached our standard security Q&A; flag any gaps.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-sketch.xlsx (high-level pilot cost sketch)

Proposed timeline
- 4/5: follow-up proposal + pilot TCO scenarios (we’ll include dedicated and hosted options)
- 4/12: decision point / procurement Q&A
- Mid-April: pilot kickoff (if approved)

If you confirm the numbers above I’ll run a conservative TCO with Ben and share three scenarios (low/medium/high usage + recommended levers to hit the $30k target).

Thanks again — enjoyed the call.

Best,

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful and captures the call. A few clarifications: 

- 120M/month is our optimistic peak. Realistically we expect 40–60M for month 1 of the pilot, ramping up to 100–120M by month 3 if the recommender index and search use expands. We do have predictable weekday peaks between 10:00–16:00 PT.
- $30k/mo is what Procurement set as their preferred cap for initial vendor pilots. We might be able to approve a one-time overage if you can show expected ROI and a strict usage throttle.
- On security: SOC2 is required. We also need a short note on data retention for embeddings and whether keys/data can be kept in our KMS.

Can you and your team run two options: (A) hosted pilot with autoscaling but strict token caps, and (B) small dedicated pool sized for our month-3 peak? We want to see cost and risk trade-offs.

If it helps I can loop in procurement next week for a 15-min call.

—Sara

Ben / Sergio — forwarding the LedgerOne recap and Sara's reply. Key asks: two cost scenarios (hosted w/ caps vs small dedicated pool sized for month-3 peak), SOC2 + KMS note, and a capped pilot price of $30k/mo preferred by procurement.

Specifics for the TCO sketch I want you to include:
- Baseline: hosted (pay-as-you-go) with continuous batching assumptions (3 batching profiles: aggressive, balanced, conservative) and expected token latency impacts.
- Dedicated: estimate GPU pool size to sustain 95th <200ms for chat plus embedding QPS for 100–120M/month. Include commit option (monthly) and burst policies.
- Quantization: recommended model variants with expected token-cost reduction and an accuracy delta estimate (we'll use small eval prompt set).

I've attached the security Q&A they asked for; please flag any red flags for the security team so we can pre-empt procurement.

Timeline: can you have a draft cost sheet and short notes by EOD 4/5? If not, earliest by 4/6. Sara said she can take a procurement call next week — would prefer to have something before that.

Thanks — Marissa
